questions.stem: A 22-year-old man attended clinic for review of a splitskin graft to a full-thickness burn on his left calf. The doctor was concerned about infection as there was worsening exudate and pain, with 2 cm erythema around the edges. A wound swab was taken, and the patient started on empirical flucloxacillin. Wound swab: 1. Staphylococcus aureus, sensitive to methicillin 2. Streptococcus pyogenes 3. Gram-positive rod, identifying as Corynebacterium diphtheriae, awaiting confirmation
questions.lead_in: What confirmatory test on organism 3 would substantially alter the management of this patient?
questions.explanation: Modified Elek test The Elek immunoprecipitation test confirms the production of diphtheria toxin. PCR tests are now also available to demonstrate presence of the diphtheria toxin genes. Diphtheria toxin production requires enhanced public health management of both the patient and their close contacts.

questions.question: A fully vaccinated girl is admitted for a femur fracture. Her brother is admitted with diphtheritic pharyngitis. Her throat swab grows Corynebacterium diphtheriae; she is asymptomatic and has no wounds.
questions.question_raw: Girl, fully vaccinated, admitted for femur fracture. Brother admitted with diphtheria pharyngitis. Girl has c. diphtheria in throat swab, asymptomatic and has no wounds.

parts.text: What precautions should she be placed on?
When can precautions be safely discontinued?
How would you manage this patient – be specific regarding antibiotics and any other measures?

parts_raw.text: What precautions to put her on
When can you safely d/c her precautions
How would you manage this patient – be specific regarding abx and whatever else you’d do

questions.model_answer: a) Droplet precautions (respiratory carriage), in addition to standard precautions; contact precautions if a cutaneous lesion were present. b) When two cultures taken at least 24 hours apart, and no earlier than 14 days after completion of antibiotic therapy, are both negative; if cultures remain positive, give erythromycin for a further 10 days and re-culture. c) (1) Treat carriage with a single dose of IM benzathine penicillin G (1.2 million U as she is ≥6 years old) OR erythromycin for 7–10 days (40 mg/kg/day, up to 1 g/day); erythromycin is preferred for eradicating the carrier state. (2) Review immunization status and give a diphtheria toxoid booster if >5 years have elapsed since her last dose (complete/initiate a primary series if history is unknown or incomplete). (3) Notify public health and obtain nasopharyngeal/throat cultures.

cohort_answer.text: When abx therapy is complete and 2 throat swab (or skin swab if lesion) cultures are negative x 2 24hrs apart.

questions.question: A 30-year-old woman is admitted for a hip fracture. Her son at home has pharyngitis and is diagnosed with Corynebacterium diphtheriae infection. She is asymptomatic, but a screening swab is positive for Corynebacterium diphtheriae.
questions.question_raw: A 30-year-old woman is admitted for a hip fracture. Her son at home has pharyngitis and is diagnosed with Corynebacterium diphtheriae infection. She is asymptomatic, but a screening swab is done and is positive for C. diphtheriae – (2019)

parts.text: What infection control precautions are required, if any?
What criteria are required to discontinue infection control precautions?
What are TWO aspects of management (list specific drug[s], if applicable)?

parts_raw.text: What infection control precautions are required, if any?
What criteria are required to discontinue infection control precautions?
What are TWO aspects of management (list specific drug[s], if applicable).

questions.model_answer: a) Droplet precautions (plus standard precautions) for respiratory carriage; contact precautions if a skin lesion is present. b) Two cultures obtained at least 24 hours apart, and no earlier than 14 days after completion of antibiotic therapy, both negative (continue erythromycin × further 10 days if still positive). c) (1) Antibiotic to eradicate carriage: single-dose IM benzathine penicillin G 1.2 million U (≥6 years) OR erythromycin 7–10 days (1 g/day for adults). (2) Assess vaccination status and give a diphtheria toxoid booster if >5 years since last dose (complete/initiate primary series if unknown or incomplete).

cohort_answer.text: Precautions: Droplet/Contact (+ Standard). Discontinue when: two consecutive cultures (separated by 24 hours) are negative. Management: antimicrobial prophylaxis - Erythromycin 250mg PO QID x7-10 days OR Penicillin G Benzathine 1.2MU IM x1 dose; assess vaccination status and update if incomplete and/or last booster not within past 5 years.

questions.question: A 6-month-old infant has diphtheria infection.

parts.text: List two infection prevention and control measures to institute immediately.
What is the main virulence factor and its mechanism?

parts_raw.text: C) What is the main virulence factor and its mechanism?

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Droplet precautions for respiratory diphtheria (contact precautions if cutaneous), maintained until two cultures ≥24 h apart and ≥14 days after completing antibiotics are negative. (2) Notify public health, culture throat/nasopharynx/lesions, and treat close contacts. b) The diphtheria exotoxin. Its catalytic fragment A ADP-ribosylates and irreversibly inactivates elongation factor 2 (EF-2), halting eukaryotic protein synthesis and killing the cell; fragment B mediates receptor binding and membrane transport. The tox gene is carried by a lysogenic corynebacteriophage.

cohort_answer.text:
Isolation (routine practices + droplet precautions for pharyngeal, or contact for cutaneous) until proof of elimination of C. diphtheriae; Report to public health. Proof of elimination: 2 consecutive negative cultures 24h apart, 24h after cessation of antibiotics. Other measures: review vaccination, NP swab cultures, immediate diphtheria toxoid dose, Pen G benzathine IM x1 for exposures (or erythromycin x7-10 days)
Tox+ strains: potent exotoxin inhibiting protein synthesis in mammals (ADP ribosylase A domain + binding B domain). Toxic effects on heart, nerves, kidneys causing myocarditis, delayed peripheral nerve conduction, ATN
